title: fix(desktop): stop the app freezing forever at start recording (uiohook-napi deadlock)
body:
Tracker: [NIW2-540](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-540) (this bug) · follow-ups [NIW2-541](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-541) utilityProcess isolation · [NIW2-545](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-545) upstream + drop the patch on 1.5.6 · [NIW2-542](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-542) flaky E2E · [NIW2-544](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-544) MaxListeners · [NIW2-543](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-543) editable cursor (idea)

Starting a recording could freeze the whole desktop app, permanently. The main process blocked inside `uIOhook.start()` of `uiohook-napi` 1.5.5 (the global mouse hook behind auto-zoom on clicks), so nothing responded, not even quit; only `kill -9` ended it. It happened twice on 2026-10-28 in normal use, on the library as shipped in 0.14.x and in the 0.15.0 candidate (#361). A `sample` of the hung process shows the main thread in `hook_enable → uv_thread_join` and the hook thread in `worker_dispatch_proc → uv_mutex_lock`: the startup handshake deadlock fixed upstream by [SnosMe/uiohook-napi#66](https://github.com/SnosMe/uiohook-napi/pull/66), open and unmerged since August. We confirmed it there: [our comment](https://github.com/SnosMe/uiohook-napi/pull/66#issuecomment-6473120620).

This PR applies that fix as a bun dependency patch (`patches/uiohook-napi@1.5.5.patch`, byte-identical to the PR's head), pins it with a regression test, and makes the "native rebuild pending" stamp notice the patch. It also corrects three places that said a skipped rebuild "degrades to no clicks": the shipped prebuild is a N-API module, Electron loads it fine, and that is exactly how the hung process was running the unpatched code.

**The mechanism, in one paragraph.** `hook_enable()` waited on a condition variable without a predicate loop and used a second mutex as an "is running" flag. On a spurious or early wakeup, `uv_mutex_trylock()` on that flag succeeded, was misread as "startup failed", and the function joined the hook thread while still holding both mutexes. The hook thread was blocked on one of them in `EVENT_HOOK_ENABLED`. Both wait forever. The patch replaces the flag with an explicit `hook_start_state` guarded by one mutex, waited on in a `while (state == PENDING)` loop, and joins without holding locks.

## What changes for you

- **Every machine and every CI job must run `bun run rebuild:native` after pulling this** (or `bun run setup` will tell you). `bun install` patches the C **sources** only; the binary that runs is the one `rebuild:native` compiles. Before this PR the stamp only tracked the Electron version, so a build from before the patch would have read as current. It now reads as pending.
- Release pipelines already call the rebuild on macOS and Windows; the Windows job's stamp check now compares Electron version **plus patch hash**.
- No change to what the hook captures (still mouse-down only), no `postinstall`, no change to `click-hook.ts`.

## What to review

1. **`patches/uiohook-napi@1.5.5.patch` — the C fix, as if it were ours.** Decide whether every exit path of `hook_thread_proc` sets `FINISHED`, whether `hook_enable()` unlocks on thread-create failure, and whether the join really runs without locks. Two independent reviews (Opus, Codex) read it; the ledger is in the first comment. Not reachable by any test: the race cannot be forced (50 000 start/stop cycles never hit it, patched or not).
2. **`scripts/native-deps-stamp.sh:25-37` — the patch hash.** One `node -e` call, cwd-relative paths, sha256 of the sorted `patches/*.patch` bytes (12 hex chars), `patches-none` when there are none. Two review rounds rewrote this for Git Bash (MSYS path conversion, `shasum` availability, `cat` reading stdin). Decide whether anything left depends on the shell: the only bash is `cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."`.
3. **`.github/workflows/release-desktop.yml:247-256` — the Windows stamp check.** It lost `working-directory` and now uses repo-relative paths. Check it matches the step before it and fails loudly on mismatch.
4. **`scripts/setup-dev.sh:92-115` — what a developer reads.** Decide whether the pending message is strong enough: "the unpatched hook runs — start() can deadlock the app".
5. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/click-hook-native-patch.test.ts:45-61` — what the test can and cannot catch.** It asserts on the *installed* sources (predicate loop present, `hook_running_mutex` absent from code). A future patch that keeps the loop but reintroduces a different race passes; say if you want a stronger invariant.

**Safe to skim:** `package.json` / `bun.lock` (written by `bun patch --commit`), `.gitattributes` (one line), `CLAUDE.md`, the comment-only edits in `scripts/rebuild-native.sh`, `pr-checks.yml`.

## Proof

Criteria were set in chat (no tracker issue existed; the Linear bug is created with this PR).

| Criterion | What was done | How to check it | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PR #66 applied via bun `patchedDependencies`, native rebuilt | `bun patch` + `bun patch --commit`, `bun run rebuild:native` | step 1 | `grep -c hook_start_state node_modules/uiohook-napi/src/lib/uiohook_worker.c` → 3; stamp `39.8.10+patches-7da4512db80a`; `build/Release/uiohook_napi.node` 87 296 B |
| Stress harness: N start/stop cycles in Electron without a hang | Electron harness, external 20 s timeout, `sample` on hang | step 2 | `[stress] OK: 50000 start/stop cycles in 6947 ms`, exit 0. **Caveat:** the unpatched prebuild also passes 50 000 cycles (5984 ms). The harness proves nothing broke, not that the race is gone; the recorded `sample` of pid 3696 is the repro, and the fix is argued from the code. |
| Desktop unit suite green | — | step 3 | `vitest run` → exit 0, 300 files, 2881 tests |
| CI green on the PR | — | PR checks | pending at open time; updated by the babysit comment |
| Regression test fails without the patch | committed red first (f1e35d52: 3 failed), green after c2a6aab6 | step 4 | `click-hook-native-patch.test.ts` 3/3 |
| Unchanged: mouse-down only, no `postinstall`, no `click-hook.ts` change | — | `git diff main...HEAD --stat` | neither file in the diff; no `postinstall` key in any `package.json` |

## Decisions

- **Patch upstream PR #66 instead of forking, using a third-party fork or writing our own hook.** Options: bun patch (taken), fork + publish `@kaipu/uiohook-napi` with prebuilds, the Valis fork tarball (0 stars, days old, pinned to Electron 45), a Rust/Swift hook like Cap/OpenScreen. Taken: the smallest reviewable change that ships the same code any fork would, chosen by the owner after the options were presented. State of the art checked: `uiohook-napi` has 92 k weekly downloads and is what every Electron recorder uses (ZoomReel, Zoomcast, Recordly); the only alternative is a native helper of our own, which only pays off together with a native capture pipeline (follow-up).
- **Patch kept byte-identical to the upstream PR head** (`74f03bb`), long comments included, so a bump re-diffs trivially and reviewers can compare with upstream.
- **Regression test asserts on files, not behavior.** A test that calls `start()` cannot trigger the race; it would be a false proof.
- **Stamp = Electron version + patch hash, computed by one script** used by the rebuild, `setup-dev.sh` and CI, instead of an mtime check (fragile across checkouts) or a second stamp file.
- **Doc/comment corrections ride along** because they are wrong about the exact mechanism this PR depends on (a skipped rebuild is *not* harmless). Reviewer may argue scope; splitting is cheap if asked.
- **Not done here, ticketed:** isolate the hook in a `utilityProcess` so no library bug can freeze the app again (the review also found a pre-existing stop-side hang: a key press during `stop()` dispatch_syncs to a main thread blocked in `uv_thread_join`); raise upstream that `FINISHED + SUCCESS` should map to failure; the three flaky Playwright E2E tests; the `MaxListenersExceededWarning` for `settings:changed`.

## Checks

- `apps/kaipu-record: node_modules/.bin/vitest run` → exit 0, 300 files / 2881 tests passed
- `apps/kaipu-record: tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.node.json` → exit 0
- root `oxlint .` → exit 0 (18 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors); `oxfmt --check .` → exit 0
- `bun scripts/check-release-workflow.ts` → exit 0; `bun scripts/check-workflow-eligibility.ts` → exit 0
- `bash -n` on the three shell scripts → ok
- Stress harness on the rebuilt binary: 50 000 cycles, exit 0 (see Proof)

None of the above compiles the C; `bun run rebuild:native` does (exit 0 locally, stamp written). The desktop E2E suite runs only on release candidates (ADR 0006/0027).

## Manual verification

- [ ] On a machine that had already run `rebuild:native` before this branch: `git pull`, `bun install`, `bun run setup` → "uiohook-napi built for 39.8.10, expected 39.8.10+patches-…" (pending), then `bun run rebuild:native` → ✓.
- [ ] Record 10 times in a row with Accessibility granted; the app never freezes at "start recording" (this never proves the absence of a 1-in-N race; it proves the patched hook starts and stops).
- [ ] Windows release job: `bun install --frozen-lockfile` applies the patch (CRLF guarded by `.gitattributes`) and the stamp check passes.

## What I did not verify

- The Windows build of the patched sources (MSVC) and `bun` 1.3.4 (CI) accepting a patch committed by bun 1.4.2 (local). Both run on the next release workflow; the PR checks run `rebuild:native` on macOS only.
- The deadlock's absence. It cannot be reproduced on demand; the fix is argued from the sampled stack and the code, and matches upstream's analysis.
- That the second hang on 2026-10-28 had the same cause: only one of the two processes was sampled.
- Linux: not a target.

## How to test it yourself

**Setup**
```bash
git fetch origin && git switch fix/uiohook-start-deadlock
bun install
bun run setup          # expect uiohook-napi: rebuild pending
bun run rebuild:native # compiles the patched C against Electron 39.8.10
bun run setup          # expect ✓ uiohook-napi built for 39.8.10+patches-7da4512db80a
```

**1. The patch reached the sources the binary was compiled from**
```bash
grep -c hook_start_state apps/kaipu-record/node_modules/uiohook-napi/src/lib/uiohook_worker.c
ls -la apps/kaipu-record/node_modules/uiohook-napi/build/Release/uiohook_napi.node
```
Expect: `3`, and a `.node` file newer than your `bun install`.
Broken if: `0`, or no `build/Release` (then the app loads `prebuilds/darwin-arm64/uiohook-napi.node`, the unpatched one).

**2. Start/stop the hook thousands of times inside Electron**
Create `/tmp/stress/main.js` with the harness from the PR comment "Stress harness" (also in the Linear issue), then:
```bash
E=apps/kaipu-record/node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron
echo '{"name":"stress","main":"main.js"}' > /tmp/stress/package.json
"$E" /tmp/stress 50000
```
Expect: `[stress] OK: 50000 start/stop cycles in <~7000> ms`, exit 0, within 20 s.
Broken if: no output and the process is still alive after 20 s → `sample <pid> 1` shows `hook_enable` / `uv_thread_join`.

**3. Unit suite**
```bash
cd apps/kaipu-record && node_modules/.bin/vitest run
```
Expect: 300 files, 2881 tests, exit 0.

**4. The regression test is real**
```bash
cd apps/kaipu-record && node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/recording/click-hook-native-patch.test.ts
sed -i '' 's/^  "patchedDependencies"/  "x-patchedDependencies"/' ../../package.json && node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/main/recording/click-hook-native-patch.test.ts; git -C ../.. checkout package.json
```
Expect: 3 passed, then 1 failed ("is declared for the installed version"), then clean tree.

**5. Record in the real app**
`bun run dev`, grant Accessibility if not already, start and stop a screen recording ten times. Expect: every start proceeds to the countdown; the app never hangs. Open the editor on one of them and confirm clicks still appear on the cursor track (auto-zoom markers).
